subject: Materials Science
title: P-Type Doping: Creating Holes
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: P-Type Doping: Creating Holes.

hook.text: Replace a silicon atom with boron — three valence electrons instead of four — and a hole appears.

buildup.text: Boron has three valence electrons. It bonds with three silicon neighbors but leaves one bond incomplete.

discovery.text: A nearby electron fills the hole, creating a new hole next door — the hole hops through the lattice.

twist.text: Holes move slower than electrons — that's why PMOS transistors are larger than NMOS in chip designs.

climax.text: CMOS logic uses both n-type and p-type together — complementary pairs that consume almost zero standby power.

punchline.text: Remove one electron and a positive ghost carries current through the crystal.

quiz.question: Why does boron create p-type silicon?
options: It adds extra electrons to the lattice
It has fewer valence electrons, creating holes as majority carriers
It increases the band gap of silicon
